scope: Question planning for 433 Biomni-Eval1 tool-enabled records in 20 families. All 100 DBQA/SeqQA stems are reviewed; the other 333 prompt structures are audited across eight protocols and six families. All families have proposed endpoint-specific contracts, but individual biological evidence, independent inputs and runtime remain unresolved. No implementation or validated coverage. The same seven database cards also receive 520 LAB-Bench DbQA schema-level targets; all remain prospective with candidate sets and biological record evidence uninspected.

defaults.data: Independent observed inputs and native data formats; preserve real biological replication and lineage. No source benchmark fixtures, expected labels or answer text used for task authoring.
defaults.consolidation: Do not instantiate one task per registry row. Split on distinct measured properties, variant classes, leakage risks or evidence requirements, then merge compatible questions across benchmarks.
defaults.authoring_status: Planning only. No implementation workers assigned.

questions.scientific_question: Which candidate variants have the strongest reproducible association evidence for an independently selected phenotype under an explicit study and ranking rule?
required_endpoint_stages: Resolve the phenotype concept, candidate variant identities, genome assembly and eligible studies.
Align each association to its actual effect allele, cohort and measured phenotype, preserving ambiguous or missing matches.
Compute the complete candidate evidence ranking using a declared statistic and study-selection rule.
Keep association strength, fine-mapping probability and functional evidence in separate fields; preserve ties and unsupported candidates.
observed_input_requirements: Observed association summary statistics or source association records, trait ontology mappings, study/cohort metadata and versioned rs-to-allele mappings. Source prompts supply a trait and rs candidates, not individual genotypes; a VCF is optional only when allele harmonization requires it.
required_formats: GWAS summary-statistic TSV or documented association export
proposed_artifact_requirements: candidate_identity.tsv: query_id, candidate_id, rs_id, assembly, chromosome, position, alleles, mapping_status
association_evidence.tsv: query_id, candidate_id, study_id, trait_id, ancestry, sample_size, effect_allele, effect_type, effect, standard_error, p_value, source_record_id
candidate_ranking.tsv: query_id, candidate_id, eligible_evidence_count, ranking_statistic, rank, tie_group, disposition
analysis_spec.json: trait matching, eligible studies, allele rules and candidate-selection criterion
source_specific_decisions: Define what strongest means before observing outcomes; do not mix p-values, fine-mapping probabilities and effect magnitudes into an unstated score.
Handle multiple cohorts and repeated publication records without pseudoreplication; related traits are not interchangeable.
Preserve p-value precision, censored values and odds-ratio versus beta semantics; ambiguous alleles must not receive invented effect directions.
deterministic_verification_approach: Use a pinned native summary-statistic parser/harmonizer and independent identity, eligibility and ranking checks. Compare all evidence rows and all candidate ranks; validate any numerical transformation with explicit tolerances.
questions.evaluation_contract: Verify complete candidate evidence and outputs under frozen scientific rules, including ambiguity, missingness and all declared selection constraints. A deterministic algorithm output does not independently establish biological causality or clinical truth.
questions.source_protocol_limits: The 43 source prompts request one associated rs identifier without specifying evidence rules. The authored rule must be explicit; reproducing a database rank does not prove a causal variant. Instance-specific source evidence and label provenance remain unreviewed.

endpoint_contract_review.review_scope: All prompt structures audited against the shared source templates; representative biological contexts and delivery descriptions reviewed. Individual association, screen and case evidence has not been reviewed. No source answer column inspected.
required_incorrect_output_checks: Rank by smallest p-value from an unrelated phenotype or incompatible study.
Flip an allele without updating effect direction.
Hide unmatched candidates or break a tie by file order.

Join separate evidence classes by study, locus, allele and biological context.
Run a pinned, explicitly chosen prioritization method or frozen model and return all candidate features and rankings.
Audit support, disagreement and missing evidence; retain three source protocol origins separately when assessing endpoint fidelity.
observed_input_requirements: Independent observed GWAS loci with versioned candidate gene mappings, credible-set or association evidence and compatible molecular/functional evidence. Preserve the lineage of every study and distinguish model predictions from observations.

questions.scientific_question: Which candidate genes have the strongest measured perturbation effect in an independently observed screen with matching experimental context?
required_endpoint_stages: Match experimental context and candidate identities to a specific observed screen.
Verify perturbation type, measured phenotype, effect direction, time point and comparison group before combining measurements.
Use published eligible effect estimates or run a specified native screen method on raw observations, retaining all candidates and uncertainty.
Rank candidates by a prespecified signed or absolute effect rule and report missing, tied or incomparable results.
observed_input_requirements: An independent published benign cellular-phenotype screen with per-gene measurements, exact assay/condition/time metadata and biological replicates. Use guide-count inputs only when a raw-screen analysis is explicitly part of the authored workflow.
proposed_artifact_requirements: context_match.tsv: query_id, screen_id, biological_system, perturbation_type, condition, time_point, measured_phenotype, match_status

source_specific_decisions: Strongest perturbation effect must specify direction, scale and relevant contrast. Largest absolute effect and strongest effect in a desired direction are different endpoints.
Do not mix assay units, times or conditions; guides are not biological replicates. A screen-method recomputation must use the same declared control/normalization design.
Choose independent benign observed contexts for authoring and retain a fidelity gap for source cases whose experimental context cannot be matched.
deterministic_verification_approach: Run the actual selected screen-analysis package when raw counts are used; otherwise parse the source measurement export natively. Independently verify context/identity joins, candidate eligibility, replicate aggregation and complete ordering.

Resolve all candidate gene identifiers and retrieve compatible annotation evidence.
Run a prespecified phenotype-prioritization method with explicit information-content and missing-data rules.
Report every candidate score and contribution, then select the permitted number of genes while retaining ambiguity.
observed_input_requirements: Permitted, independently observed phenotype case records or phenopackets, versioned HPO ontology and phenotype-gene/disease annotations, plus candidate identifiers. Do not manufacture a patient by sampling terms from a known diagnosis. Source input contains no patient VCF.

Freeze ontology closure, information-content corpus, term weighting, negation/frequency treatment, score method and candidate cardinality. Lack of a reported phenotype does not mean it is absent.

questions.scientific_question: Which delivery-method comparisons are supported by independently published measurements in a matched biological context under explicit outcome criteria?
required_endpoint_stages: Resolve biological context and the exact outcome to compare.
Assess whether observed methods were compared under compatible assay designs and retain noncomparability.
Compute a declared comparative statistic or constrained ranking from measured outcomes, retaining uncertainty and tradeoffs.
Report the evidence-supported choice, tie or insufficient-evidence result without inventing a universally optimal category.
observed_input_requirements: Independent published benign assay measurements with cell/tissue context, delivery category, measured editing/delivery outcome, viability and study design. A context label alone is insufficient; no fabricated comparative performance measurements.

Define measured endpoint, comparability rules and decision constraints before inspecting rankings. Different outcomes can imply different choices; allow unresolved tradeoffs.
Two source IDs have identical prompt text; keep their identities without counting them as two independent contexts.
deterministic_verification_approach: Use a pinned native statistical package for the declared observed-outcome comparison and independently check units, replicate identities, normalization, complete candidate comparisons and decision rules. No model judge or canned cell-type-to-category lookup.

questions.scientific_question: What complete restriction-fragment multiset follows from independently observed DNA records under explicit topology and cleavage conventions?
required_endpoint_stages: Parse full input sequences and topology; resolve every requested enzyme to its recognition and cleavage definitions.
Enumerate oriented recognition sites and all associated cleavage events, including cuts outside recognition motifs and enzymes with two double-strand cuts.
Combine coincident events under the declared rule and derive every fragment, preserving order, lengths and repeated lengths.
Report both the fragment multiset and requested count/length summaries with source-sequence identity.
observed_input_requirements: Accessioned benign DNA in FASTA/GenBank with known topology and a pinned enzyme-definition snapshot; select independent sequences without planting recognition sites.
required_formats: BED-like interbase cut coordinates with explicit schema
proposed_artifact_requirements: cuts.tsv: sequence_id, enzyme, recognition_start, recognition_strand, cleavage_event_id, top_cut, bottom_cut, boundary_status
fragments.tsv: sequence_id, fragment_id, left_event, right_event, wraparound, length_convention, length
fragments.fasta: every product under the declared reference-strand representation
summary.tsv: sequence_id, enzyme_set, physical_fragment_count, sorted_lengths_with_multiplicity
source_specific_decisions: Topology, complete-digestion model, methylation assumption, ambiguous-base handling and sequence-end exclusions.
A cut coordinate is not a recognition-site start. Freeze top/bottom cleavage geometry and the length convention for staggered ends.
Physical fragments, distinct lengths and visible gel bands differ; the source does not supply a gel-resolution model. Do not silently grade unique lengths as fragment count.
Two-cut enzymes and circular origin-spanning sites need explicit support or an uncovered endpoint disposition.
deterministic_verification_approach: Run pinned Bio.Restriction for recognized sites and cleavage definitions; independently enumerate strand-aware interbase events and fragment lengths. Compare full event and fragment multisets, including multiplicity, and conservation under the stated length convention.
questions.evaluation_contract: Require all specified input-dependent artifacts and all query modes claimed as covered. Preserve multiplicity, ambiguity and full candidate outcomes; compare native outputs with independently computed checks. No benchmark answer labels or LLM judge.
questions.source_protocol_limits: The source contains four length and three count questions. A motif-count shortcut misses cleavage geometry. This is a computational complete-digest model; methylation, partial digestion and observed gel migration are not established by a sequence oracle.

endpoint_contract_review.runtime_boundary: Bound observed input selection by scientific scope; native reference and solver runtime must be measured before claiming <=30-minute completion.

questions.scientific_question: Which complete ORFs, translated products and requested residues follow from independently observed DNA under a fully specified ORF definition?
required_endpoint_stages: Enumerate eligible strands and reading frames using the declared start, stop, partial-ORF and nested-start rules.
Translate every eligible ORF and retain genomic coordinates, frame, completeness and protein length.
Apply the source endpoint mode: strict length threshold, longest-protein selection or an indexed amino acid in a longest ORF.
Retain tied longest ORFs and out-of-range residues under explicit answer rules.
observed_input_requirements: Independently observed genomic or transcript sequences in FASTA with species, topology and matching genetic-code metadata. Preserve native record identifiers and original lengths.
required_formats: GFF3 or explicit ORF coordinate TSV
proposed_artifact_requirements: orfs.tsv: sequence_id, orf_id, strand, frame, start, end, wraps_origin, start_codon, stop_codon, completeness, protein_length
proteins.fasta: all eligible ORF translations keyed by orf_id

source_specific_decisions: Choose start-to-stop versus stop-to-stop ORFs; allowed starts, both-strand search, partial boundaries, circular wrap and genetic code must be specified in the task.
Freeze nested start handling, whether initiator codons are translated as methionine, and whether terminal stop is excluded from amino-acid length.
The two count questions say greater than, not at least. Preserve strict inequality, one-based requested residue positions and a nonarbitrary tie policy.
deterministic_verification_approach: Run pinned EMBOSS getorf with explicit options, then independently validate start/stop coordinates and codon translation with Biopython. Compare the full ORF set and all query modes; first check that native getorf settings express the chosen nested-start/partial rules.

Construct each complete product with primer-derived sequence where specified and compute its full length.
For candidate-selection modes, compare complete sequence or length as requested; for given-pair modes, retain ambiguity and all qualifying products.
